card: Updates lint-shell.py to automatically inspect any repository file containing a shell shebang instead of only files matching *.sh or hardcoded Guix paths. It also enables shellcheck rule SC2162 and updates read invocations across several shell scripts to use read -r. The change ensures non-.sh shell scripts receive automated shellcheck coverage in CI.
evidence: PR description: "The current shellcheck lint silently ignores all files with a shell shebang that are not ending in `.sh`. Fix it by linting them, which also simplifies the script, because manually appending of guix scripts can be dropped."
Commit fa439e438c: "None of the read calls are expected to parse backslash escapes. Use `read -r` to preserve literal backslashes if they occur."
problem: Shell scripts without a `.sh` file extension (such as `ci/retry/retry` or init scripts) silently bypassed shellcheck unless manually hardcoded into the linter script. Additionally, suppressing SC2162 globally allowed `read` commands across scripts to mangle literal backslashes.

risk.why: Touches only linting scripts and minor shell script helper invocations without affecting consensus, node operations, or release binaries.

summary: Updates the shellcheck linter in `test/lint/lint-shell.py` to detect and lint any repository file starting with a shell shebang, rather than only files ending in `.sh` and hardcoded Guix paths. It also removes the repository-wide shellcheck suppression for SC2162 (`read -r`) and fixes resulting lint warnings across several repository shell scripts.
